story.headline: AiMOGA Robotics Unveils Consumer Humanoid Companion Robot 'Mobo'
story.summary: Chery Group's robotics brand AiMOGA officially debuted Mobo, a consumer-grade home companion humanoid robot, opening international pre-orders during the 2026 EXEED International User Summit. The robot is designed for everyday household interactions and personal assistance.

keyTakeaways: AiMOGA Robotics is launching Mobo, a consumer humanoid companion robot powered by its proprietary MoAgent AI system.

draft.body:
AiMOGA Robotics, the intelligent robotics brand of Chinese automaker Chery Group, is stepping into the consumer market with Mobo, its first humanoid companion robot designed specifically for family households. According to an announcement via [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/17/3382868/0/en/aimoga-to-unveil-mobo-its-first-family-companion-robot-on-october-21.html), the company is hosting the formal debut and opening worldwide pre-orders on October 21, 2026, in Wuhu, Anhui. The launch takes place during the 2026 Chery International User Summit, running October 19 through October 23, where Chery is showcasing how automotive manufacturing and embodied artificial intelligence intersect in everyday living.

Mobo previously appeared in public exhibitions at both the World Robot Conference and the World Manufacturing Convention. Its commercial rollout marks a deliberate pivot for AiMOGA, moving from enterprise service deployments into personal living spaces where machines must negotiate unscripted human routines.

## MoAgent Architecture and Household Capabilities

At the center of Mobo's software stack is MoAgent, a proprietary AI architecture developed by AiMOGA. As detailed by [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/16/3382702/0/en/aimoga-to-launch-home-companion-robot-mobo-and-open-global-pre-orders-at-2026-chery-international-user-summit.html), MoAgent is designed to parse multi-part spoken instructions, break them into sequential actions, and plan long-horizon tasks rather than behaving like a conventional single-prompt voice assistant. The system connects multimodal perception, conversation, and mechanical execution to support continuous, goal-oriented domestic help.

Mobo is equipped with spatial sensing and visual object recognition, allowing it to evaluate indoor surroundings, understand physical relationships between items, and navigate domestic layouts using dynamic obstacle avoidance. AiMOGA reports that the robot maintains long-term memory, enabling it to remember individual family members' habits, schedules, and preferences across ongoing conversations. The company added that privacy protections have been incorporated into the system's architecture from the outset.

Physically, Mobo operates on a full-body motion system providing 22 degrees of freedom. AiMOGA stated that this actuation allows the humanoid robot to perform expressive gestures, maintain stable movement, and execute coordinated dance routines for interactive entertainment and child learning.

[[FIG1]]

## Automotive Engineering Meets Domestic Humanoids

AiMOGA's path to consumer hardware differs from that of pure-play robotics startups because of its direct integration with Chery Group's industrial footprint. As reported by [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/17/3382868/0/en/aimoga-to-unveil-mobo-its-first-family-companion-robot-on-october-21.html), the robotics brand utilizes Chery's global research network and supply chain infrastructure, drawing on 31 internal research laboratories focused on intelligent perception and advanced motion control.

The hardware transfers technologies originally built for automotive smart cockpits and autonomous driving systems into robotic frames. This cross-discipline pipeline uses CheryMind, an automotive-specific large AI model, to accelerate robotic perception and contextual reasoning. Coverage from [Humanoid Robotics Technology](https://humanoidroboticstechnology.com/industry-news/aimoga-to-unveil-new-home-robot-at-chery-international-user-summit-2026/) notes that Chery plans further technical alignment between AiMOGA and its LUXEED smart cockpit ecosystem, pursuing shared software links among vehicles, smart home infrastructure, and personal robots.

AiMOGA already holds CE certification in the European Union and FCC compliance in the United States, giving its hardware regulatory clearance across key international territories.

## Portfolio Demonstration Across Real-World Sectors

While Mobo serves as AiMOGA's consumer flagship, the company's broader operational portfolio is being demonstrated throughout the summit at the Chery Global Technology Innovation Center. According to reporting from [The AI Insider](https://theaiinsider.tech/2026/10/17/aimoga-to-open-global-pre-orders-for-mobo-home-humanoid-robot/), AiMOGA's robots are already operating across more than 100 enterprise use cases, having accumulated more than 3,000 commercial deliveries across 60 countries and regions.

[[FIG2]]

The company set up functional trial zones at the summit to showcase how distinct form factors address specific industry demands:

* **Public Safety and Traffic:** Dedicated traffic police robots demonstrate patrol functions and traffic guidance routines.
* **Healthcare Navigation:** The Robotic Nurse system interacts with visitors to provide medical guidance and visitor guidance in clinical station mockups.
* **Retail and Commerce:** The Mornine humanoid acts as an autonomous presenter inside checkout-free grocery displays and livestreaming stations.
* **Logistics and Carrying:** The Argos and Argos Pro quadruped robots perform autonomous trailing and cargo transport tests.
* **Home Living:** Mobo conducts interactive communication, schedule management, and educational activities geared toward children and multi-generational households.

## Pricing, Delivery Timelines, and Commercial Outlook

Although global pre-orders open October 21, critical commercial details remain unannounced. As industry tracker [WittyWires](https://wittywires.com/forums/topic/aimoga-opens-global-pre-orders-for-mobo-home-humanoid-robot/) observed, AiMOGA did not disclose Mobo's retail price, deposit requirements, or expected delivery schedules during its initial summit briefings.

Opening pre-orders without published hardware pricing or delivery targets keeps Mobo in an introductory phase. While AiMOGA's reported delivery of 3,000 commercial robots demonstrates mature manufacturing backing, transitioning a 22-degree-of-freedom humanoid into homes requires navigating unpredictable domestic spaces, strict consumer privacy standards, and cost barriers. The forthcoming demonstrations during the Wuhu summit are expected to clarify how quickly Chery intends to move Mobo from exhibition floors to consumer living rooms.

faq.q: What is Mobo and who makes it?
faq.a: Mobo is a consumer-grade humanoid companion robot developed by AiMOGA Robotics, an intelligent robotics brand owned by China's Chery Group.

faq.q: What makes Mobo's software different from traditional smart assistants?
faq.a: Mobo runs on AiMOGA's proprietary MoAgent AI system, which combines spatial perception, visual object recognition, and multimodal interaction to break complex requests into steps and execute long-horizon household tasks.

faq.q: How much does Mobo cost and when will it ship?
faq.a: AiMOGA has not publicly disclosed pricing, reservation deposit amounts, or scheduled shipping dates, despite opening global pre-orders on October 21, 2026.

faq.q: What other robots does AiMOGA manufacture?
faq.a: AiMOGA's fleet includes the Mornine retail robot, the Argos and Argos Pro quadruped robots, hospital navigation robots, and automated traffic police robots.
